pricing.rule: Each delivered call bills price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005. A pending/async ack or an unverifiable charged call (delivered:false, refundable:false) bills price_usd × 1.15 with no per-call fee; refunded calls, in-batch duplicates and failed runs bill $0. A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

comment.comment:
My bullish thesis on $TeleMoney is pretty simple: they’re building around where crypto already spends its time—X and Telegram.

This latest update is what caught my attention. The plan is to let someone launch a coin straight from a post or reply, tag whoever should receive the creator fees, and have those fees routed to Telegram. If they ship that smoothly, a meme or viral conversation could become a launch without everyone jumping through a bunch of hoops. That’s a setup I can see creators and communities actually using.

The part that makes $TM interesting to me is how they say the revenue connects back to holders: 75% distributed in SOL and 25% used for buybacks and burns. If usage grows and that model works as described, there’s a reason for holders to care about the platform succeeding beyond the next green candle.

Obviously, an announcement still needs to turn into a product people keep using. I want to see the X integration live, consistent launches, and verifiable payouts. But the direction makes sense to me: easier launches, a reason for creators to participate, and a revenue model that includes holders.

That’s why I’m holding and paying attention. Execution and adoption are what would make this thesis play out.
